key_insight: The best system scored 0.7389 on patient-specific phenotype recognition, exceeding the baseline by 8.37 percentage points.
clinical_relevance: Linking phenotype concepts to the correct patients in biomedical literature could support rare disease research and genotype–phenotype analysis, but clinical utility was not evaluated.
method: Recognize phenotype concepts in full-text biomedical articles.
Associate identified phenotypes with specific patients.
Evaluate systems exploring biomedical language models, LLMs, and ensembles.
evidence_signal: The shared task used 200 annotated PatientPheX articles covering 506 patients, 15,193 phenotype mentions, and 5,656 patient–phenotype associations.
watch_item: Patient attribution and phenotype normalization remain challenging, especially in articles describing multiple patients.
paper_title: Overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1: Patient-Specific Phenotype Concept Recognition in Full-Text Biomedical Literature
